# Wild Lake Studio | Sovereign A&R & Artist Development

> Wild Lake Studio, known as Wild-Lake, is an existential mechanics studio providing structural design and talent architecture for independent artists. Based across New York and Santiago, Dominican Republic; working worldwide.

Wild-Lake is point zero for starmaking.

## Practice and engagement

The core offering is undivided attention. Close study of the artist, the work, and the conditions shaping both. We observe, listen, and stay with the material long enough to offer a precise response.

We scout talent and work with artists directly, or partner with record labels, galleries, and booking agencies. In either case, the artist enters the engagement willingly, on their own initiative or through a representative.

Artist Development works with the creator behind the work. Creative Development works with raw material across mediums and stages. Audience development, critical writing, and channels of encounter are creative infrastructure.

The Stewardship Subscription reserves availability between client-triggered interventions. Focused observation and editing alternate with periods of independent execution. Scope, response times, and reserved capacity are agreed in advance. Fixed project commissions and focused advisory engagements are also available.

Artists retain ownership and creative control. The studio takes no percentage of artist earnings. The studio retains its proprietary frameworks and licenses delivered framework materials for the client’s practice; public-facing writing transfers to the client upon final settlement. Refer to the Terms of Practice for the full agreement boundaries.

## Founder: the medium

Argelys Samuel Oriach is a Dominican-born systems architect, performance artist, artist developer, and artistic director based in Crown Heights, Brooklyn. He constructs systems and inhabits them. Performance is the governing method of his practice; writing, voice, movement, design, and corporate roles are its forms.

Wild-Lake formalizes his fifteen-year independent practice, beginning in his freshman year at Wesleyan University with initiation into the Eclectic Society. He has guided twelve or more developing and independent multidisciplinary artists through structural stewardship and live production architecture.

He was raised in the Dominican Republic by a mother who is a housekeeper and writer and a father who is a facility maintainer and musician. At eleven, he taught himself 3D design software to draft his parents’ home; an architect later used that file for construction. He attended Phillips Academy Andover and Northwestern University’s National High School Institute (Cherubs) theatre program in 2010, playing Nick in a stage adaptation of The Handmaid’s Tale.

A method actor trained in the Alexander Technique, he describes his corporate roles as an undercover durational performance undertaken to build his life out of poverty while studying how complex systems scale from within. His work includes Cynthia Nixon’s 2018 New York gubernatorial campaign, VinePair, Kickstarter, and CookUnity. He is principal at Seven Eighty Three, the executive systems laboratory for which Wild-Lake is the foundational research site.

He majored in English at Wesleyan University, took extensive coursework in studio art and critical theory. His thesis, Breaking the circle of the plantation: Violence, affect and the ephemeral in Junot Díaz’s Afro-Caribbean literary imagination, reads The Brief Wondrous Life of Oscar Wao as an alternative archive of the diaspora through queer theory, performance studies, affect studies, and critical race theory.

Performance is his governing artistic method. “Multidisciplinary” describes the range of media; “performance artist” describes how he inhabits and works through them. His forms include writing, voice, movement, design, visual art, acting, and corporate roles. He sang with Ebony Singers and studied African drumming at Wesleyan. His writing uses a maximalist, automatic, and lyrical stream-of-consciousness style. He wrote This Is Not a Love Story (Yankees) and is writing a pilot, a one-act play, and the debut autofiction novel Graduation.

Investigation, experimentation, emotional clarity, and invitation are his personal reflective framework. Architect and shaman are personal interpretive archetypes, separate from professional credentials.

## The Method: the manual

Terms of the practice: https://wildlakestudio.com/method/#method-terms

Structural Design: How we organize the conditions around the work—time, space, resources, habits, and boundaries—so the practice can sustain what the artist wants to make.

Talent Architecture: How we develop and support the person carrying the work: their judgment, capacity, autonomy, and relationships.

Sovereign A&R: How we scout talent and develop creative material through critique, direction, and critical framing, while the artist retains ownership and creative control.

The Method describes critique and revision, structural honesty (conversational brutalism), the observer mandate, and the alternating rhythm of intervention and absence. Clients arrive to build a practice or rebuild operations that have become unsustainable. Artist wellbeing includes support for artists healing from narcissistic abuse, examining narcissistic patterns in themselves, or navigating both. The focus is self-trust, relational patterns, boundaries, and creative autonomy, with the artist deciding what to share. Wild-Lake supports artistic practice and leaves room for care beyond the studio.

As artist developers, Wild-Lake works with curators as a defensive buffer between artists and institutional demands, establishing boundaries around access, output, and carrying capacity.

Development Protocols are optional, guided practices within an agreed retained engagement: active listening, structural honesty, reading assignments, automatic writing, brainstorming, manifestation (including vision boarding), tarot readings, attentive listening to music, meditation, gentle breathwork, consensual nervous system co-regulation with ongoing consent and agreed boundaries, placement of hands, vision quests, dancing, shaking the body, crying and vocal expression. Artists may pause, decline, or change direction. These are artist development practices; no clinical qualification or guaranteed treatment outcome is stated.

Vision quests may involve a local park, the Blue Ridge Mountains, or Santiago and its surrounding campo, where the founder’s family is rooted. His lived experience grounds conversations about labor, access, and the conditions supporting creative practice.

## Past and current clients

The roster includes past and current engagements and does not imply every engagement is active. Profiles describe each practice from Wild-Lake’s perspective. Interpretation is the studio’s reading, not necessarily the artist’s stated intention. Locations belong in full biographies and profile details, not in introductory role lists.

- [Aissa Rose Gueye](https://wildlakestudio.com/clients/#aissa-gueye): Senegalese-American writer-director, creative director, actress, and model. Her practice spans film, photography, writing, and performance. Lives and works: New York / Los Angeles.
- [Argelys Samuel Oriach](https://wildlakestudio.com/clients/#argelys-oriach): Dominican-born visual, performance, and movement artist, artistic director, actor, writer, vocalist, songwriter, and the author of This Is Not a Love Story . Currently writing a pilot, a play, and his debut autofiction novel, Graduation . Lives and works: New York.
- [Drew Rutland](https://wildlakestudio.com/clients/#drew-rutland): Producer, fashion designer, and stylist working with high-profile talent and fashion brands. His background spans VIP and influencer relations, event production, and fashion design. Lives and works: New York.
- [Emily Wilson](https://wildlakestudio.com/clients/#emily-wilson): Food writer, photographer, and author of The Angel , an IACP Award-winning newsletter about food, restaurants, and the people who shape how we eat. Lives and works: New York.
- [Jessica Wilson](https://wildlakestudio.com/clients/#jessica-wilson): Multidisciplinary artist exploring how virtual systems register in bodies, objects, and everyday infrastructure. Lives and works: New York / Amsterdam.
- [Jimmy Andrew O’Keeffe](https://wildlakestudio.com/clients/#jimmy-andrew-okeeffe): Producer and filmmaker at North Six. His work includes projects for Nike and Frédéric Malle, and he produced The Sun Is In My Eyes (2024). Lives and works: New York.
- [Jordy Oriach](https://wildlakestudio.com/clients/#jordy-oriach): Left-handed power. An unconventional path from the Dominican Republic through junior college, New Mexico, and the University of Georgia. Built through persistence and progression. Lives and works: New York.
- [Kyle Roach](https://wildlakestudio.com/clients/#kyle-roach): Actor for stage and screen and model with a background in music production at Capitol Records. Lives and works: New York.
- [Patrick Schlotterback](https://wildlakestudio.com/clients/#patrick-schlotterback): Artist working in fibers and ceramics. A Studio Technician at Brooklyn Clay since 2016, his practice brings material work together with the technical infrastructure of the studio. Lives and works: New York.
- [Sophia Jennings](https://wildlakestudio.com/clients/#sophia-jennings): Writer and filmmaker. Director of Story at MakeMake, working across film, editorial, and advertising. Lives and works: Los Angeles.
- [Timo Sassen](https://wildlakestudio.com/clients/#timo-sassen): Antwerp-born fashion designer working in swimwear and now developing a full collection. His practice brings hands-on construction to clothing made for bodily expression. Lives and works: New York.
- [Zachary Reed Kantor](https://wildlakestudio.com/clients/#zachary-reed-kantor): Design director and musician. Working across product, branding, graphic, and motion design, he leads design at GIPHY. Lives and works: New York.

Emily Wilson is also a photographer; she studied photography alongside a double major in English and Sociology at Wesleyan. Sophia Jennings co-wrote and co-directed Sparks (2025) with Jake Davies; film information: https://www.instagram.com/sparks_thefilm/. Jimmy Andrew O’Keeffe produced The Sun Is In My Eyes (2024), directed and co-produced by Pablo Tapia Pla. Timo Sassen is developing a full collection after working in swimwear; source profile: https://gayletter.com/timo-sassen/.

## Quiet Creek magazine and tools

Quiet Creek is Wild-Lake’s magazine, not a separate agency. Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/quietcreekmag/. Its first essay, The Infrastructure Has an Inner Life, was published November 4, 2026 as the studio’s reading of Jessica Wilson’s work. Fountain (Weeping Outlet), 2024 is the cover; The Commute, 2025 and Siren, 2026 appear inline. Images supplied by diez gallery. The essay discusses infrastructure, attention, capitalism, whiteness, and the living world; those interpretations should not be presented as the artist’s declared themes.

Legacy /blog/ URLs redirect to /magazine/. Architectural Mirror is a simple one-to-four-card browser tool with notes and export. Quiet Creek Tarot is the separate installable, offline-capable app at https://mirror.wildlakestudio.com/app/. Readings stay on the device; no account or sign-in is required. These tools are distinct from the magazine.

## Responsibility and governance

Wild-Lake states that a fraction of every studio retainer supports freshwater defense, lake protection, and public land conservation. No percentage or recipient organization is specified. Terms of Practice cover retainers and fixed project fees, client IP, studio framework licensing, confidentiality, environmental allocation, and New York jurisdiction.

The website uses self-hosted fonts, styles, scripts, and native browser interactions. No Spotify embed, remote font request, or third-party analytics script is shipped. External services are reached through ordinary links. Hosting is provided by Cloudflare. The contact form prepares a draft in the visitor’s email app; it does not submit to a studio database.

## Names and contact

Wild Lake Studio is the formal name used for titles, legal notices, and structured data. Wild-Lake is the editorial name and wordmark. The legal entity is Wild Lake Studio LLC. Seven Eighty Three and Universe API are distinct from Wild-Lake; Universe API is a systems design framework, not a callable web API.
